rationale: B wins because it finds the fourth real story A left on the floor: "Who is responsible for a flight when no one is flying it?" That is a legitimate aviation-regulation angle sitting directly inside "no pilot," not a decorative safety panic. A is strong, but "A US drone maker bets the grid will pay a premium to avoid Chinese hardware" smuggles in a pricing premise the update does not give. B is cleaner strategy for a founder because its angles are distinct without needing that little sales-deck leap.
gaps_in_A: "bets the grid will pay a premium" invents willingness to pay and price premium before the facts earn it.
"no named utility willing to say so" overstates the release; the update says no named utility is disclosed, not that utilities refused.

"The safety case: what happens when an unpiloted drone fails over a live substation" is refused too broadly. The failure-mode framing is too hot, but a rules/accountability angle is absolutely pitchable from "no pilot."
"first concrete evidence of where the 2024 exit led" assumes this launch is the first proof point after the consumer exit; the update does not say that.
gaps_in_B: "regulators have been slow to accommodate" brings in outside context not supplied in the update. Probably true, but not proven here.
"bought and budgeted like a sensor installation" is a smart hypothesis, but it needs pricing/procurement proof before it can carry a pitch.
"Without a named utility this angle cannot be pitched" is a little absolutist; it cannot be pitched as a customer story, but the launch itself still has a narrow trade-news path.
"defense-and-security trade" risks beat creep unless the import-restriction hook is genuinely active this week.
